Now I understand the situation. The agent spent all 50 steps searching for a kettle but never found it because it only checked a limited set of locations (countertops 1-2, cabinets 1-2, drawer 1, stoveburners 1-2, coffeemachine 1, sinkbasin 1). The kettle must be in one of the unvisited locations (stoveburners 3-6, cabinets 3-9, drawers 2-13, etc.).

The core failure is that the agent never checked stoveburner 3 (or other stoveburners 4-6), which is a very common location for kettles. Additionally, even if the agent had found the kettle, it never executed the pick/clean/place actions.

Let me write a minimal corrected action sequence that:
1. Checks a new location (stoveburner 3) where the kettle is likely to be
2. Picks up the kettle
3. Cleans it at the sinkbasin
4. Places it in a cabinet
